rubric: LEARNING RUST / APPLIED: OPERATING SYSTEMS / CHAPTER 40

slides.title: Rust and the operating system
slides.main: Files, processes, and sockets are standard library types, and the ideas are the same as in the OS course.

items.title: Processes
items.sub: Args as a list, exit codes

slides.title: Files
slides.main: Short functions are thin wrappers over system calls; each returns a Result.

slides.title: Read, Write, and buffers
slides.main: File, socket, and in-memory buffer share one interface; a buffer cuts the number of system calls.

slides.title: Paths
slides.main: A path is not a string: name, extension, parent, and components are methods.

slides.title: Walking a directory
slides.main: Entry order depends on the file system: sort for reproducibility.

slides.title: I/O error kinds
slides.main: Match on the error kind and print a clear message instead of an errno number.

slides.title: Environment and exit codes
slides.main: 0 is success, anything else is an error: shell conditionals and CI rely on it.

slides.title: Launching programs
slides.main: Args as a list, not a shell string; stdout and stderr apart; exit code from status.

slides.title: Pipes between processes
slides.main: Closing the input tells the program "no more data"; otherwise it waits forever.

slides.title: TCP: echo server
slides.main: Port 0 is any free port; server in its own thread, client reads until close.

slides.title: A protocol over TCP
slides.main: TCP is a byte stream without message boundaries: the protocol needs its own (here, a newline).

slides.title: UDP and timeouts
slides.main: Bound every network wait with a timeout, or a hung neighbor will freeze your program.

slides.title: Chapter summary
slides.main: I/O in Rust means Result, the Read/Write traits, and explicit error kinds.
